t: You're standing at St Botolph-without-Bishopsgate, a Church of England church just outside where the City's eastern wall once ran, which puts it in the East End as well as the City. It takes its name from Saint Botolph, patron saint of boundaries, trade and travel, which suits a church beside a city gate. Several notable people are buried here: the mathematician John Machin, who computed pi to a hundred decimal places, Bishop John Lake, and John Welsh of Irongray, a leading Scottish Covenanter minister.
